items.label: Algorithm 1.1.1
items.statement:
Algorithm 1.1.1: A trajectory of the relaxed two-block ADMM method for a
closed proper convex linearly constrained problem. The penalty `β` and
multiplier factor `γ` are positive. The first update minimizes with `y k`, the
second minimizes with the already updated `x (k + 1)`, and only the multiplier
update contains `γ`.
items.title: Algorithm 1.1.1

items.label: Definition 2.1.1
items.statement:
Definition 2.1.1 (1): the KKT set and its three defining conditions.

Definition 2.1.1 (2): the optimal value of the constrained problem.

Definition 2.1.1 (3): the primal residual `A (x k) + B (y k) - b`.

Definition 2.1.1 (4): the second-block increment `B (y k - y (k - 1))` for `1 ≤ k`.

Definition 2.1.1 (5): a well-defined exact trajectory has finite attained block minima
at every step and obeys the multiplier update. Its initialization and all choices among
minimizers are arbitrary; nonemptiness of the KKT set does not imply block attainment.
items.title: Definition 2.1.1

items.label: Theorem 2.1.2
items.statement:
Theorem 2.1.2 (1): for an exact ADMM trajectory with closed proper convex
objectives, a KKT solution, `0 < β`, and `0 < γ ≤ 377 / 200`, the first
constraint images converge.

Theorem 2.1.2 (2): under the same hypotheses, the second constraint images
of the exact ADMM trajectory converge.

Theorem 2.1.2 (3): under the same hypotheses, the primal residuals of the
exact ADMM trajectory tend to zero.

Theorem 2.1.2 (4): under the same hypotheses, the second-block image
increments of the exact ADMM trajectory tend to zero.

Theorem 2.1.2 (5): under the same hypotheses, the objective values of the
exact ADMM trajectory tend to the constrained optimal value.

Theorem 2.1.2 (6): under the same hypotheses, the multiplier sequence of
the exact ADMM trajectory converges to an optimal multiplier.

Theorem 2.1.2 (7): if both constraint maps are injective, then under the
same hypotheses the complete primal-dual trajectory converges to a KKT triple.
items.title: Theorem 2.1.2

items.label: Theorem 2.1.3 / Theorem 2.1.4
items.statement:
Theorem 2.1.3 (1): fixed compact convex polytopes give exact-period
counterexamples for every multiplier factor at least `criticalFactor`.

Theorem 2.1.3 (2): at `criticalFactor`, smooth strongly convex objectives
with globally Lipschitz derivatives admit a period-`48` consensus ADMM
trajectory of constant positive objective value, while the origin is their
unique primal optimum of value zero and forms a KKT triple.

Theorem 2.1.3 (3): finite closed convex piecewise-quadratic objectives at
`criticalFactor` admit a period-`48` consensus ADMM trajectory of constant
positive objective value, while the origin is KKT and has optimal value zero.

Theorem 2.1.3 (4): a distinct pair of finite closed convex
piecewise-quadratic objectives gives geometric residual and objective growth.

Theorem 2.1.4 (1): one fixed pair of compact convex polytopes in ℝ⁹⁶
supports, for every multiplier factor at least ConsensusADMM.criticalFactor,
a unique-update consensus ADMM trajectory of exact period 48 and constant
positive residual.

Theorem 2.1.4 (2): at ConsensusADMM.criticalFactor, smooth strongly
convex objectives on ℝ⁹⁶ with globally Lipschitz derivatives have a
unique-update period-48 trajectory of constant positive objective value,
while the origin is their unique primal optimum of value zero and forms a KKT
triple.

Theorem 2.1.4 (3): finite closed convex piecewise-quadratic objectives at
ConsensusADMM.criticalFactor support a unique-update period-48 trajectory with
constant positive objective value, while the origin is KKT and has optimal
value zero.

Theorem 2.1.4 (4): another pair of finite closed convex
piecewise-quadratic objectives at ConsensusADMM.criticalFactor has uniquely
attained ADMM updates whose residual and objective values grow geometrically;
the origin is again KKT and has optimal value zero.
items.title: Theorem 2.1.3 / Theorem 2.1.4

items.label: Definition 2.1.5
items.statement:
Definition 2.1.5 (1): `ADMM.UniformConvergenceAt γ` requires the rank-free
convergence conclusions for every admissible exact trajectory and convergence to
a KKT triple when both constraint matrices have full column rank. Rank-free image
convergence is an additional conclusion and is not part of this predicate.

Definition 2.1.5 (2): `ADMM.uniformConvergenceEndpoint` is the supremum of
positive endpoints whose strict positive prefixes satisfy uniform convergence.
items.title: Definition 2.1.5

items.label: Corollary 2.1.6
items.statement:
Corollary 2.1.6: The uniform-convergence endpoint lies strictly between
`377 / 200` and the critical factor.
items.title: Corollary 2.1.6

items.label: Definition 3.1.1
items.statement:
Definition 3.1.1. Put `q = A.mulVec x`, `v = B.mulVec y - b`, and
`u = β⁻¹ • λ`.
The functions `ADMM.ImageReduction.fiberInf` and
`ADMM.ImageReduction.shiftedFiberInf` are the image objectives on the fibers
`A.mulVec x = q` and `B.mulVec y - b = v`, respectively. Their β-scaled Fenchel
biconjugates are `ADMM.ImageReduction.reducedFirst` and
`ADMM.ImageReduction.reducedSecond`; biconjugation is needed because an image
objective need not be closed.
items.title: Definition 3.1.1

items.label: Lemma 3.1.2
items.statement:
Lemma 3.1.2 (1): the first reduced objective is closed proper convex.

Lemma 3.1.2 (2): the second reduced objective is closed proper convex.

Lemma 3.1.2 (3): the reduced problem has a KKT triple.

Lemma 3.1.2 (4): the reduced optimal value is the original value divided by `β`.

Lemma 3.1.2 (5): first-block image values agree through biconjugation.

Lemma 3.1.2 (6): second-block image values agree through biconjugation.

Lemma 3.1.2 (7): the first image update is a relational proximal point.

Lemma 3.1.2 (8): the second image update is a relational proximal point.

Lemma 3.1.2 (9): the scaled multiplier obeys the image-update recurrence.
items.title: Lemma 3.1.2

items.label: Notation 3.1.3
items.statement:
Notation 3.1.3: the reduced KKT normalization, scaled recurrence, generated graph
normals, and support bounds are exposed by the following canonical declarations.
items.title: Notation 3.1.3

items.label: Definition 3.1.4
items.statement:
Definition 3.1.4: An ADMM finite-memory certificate consists of its nonnegative
lag weights, positive parameters, signed-value storage, and the descent and lower
finite positive-semidefiniteness tests, including all directed origin gaps.
items.title: Definition 3.1.4

items.label: Lemma 3.1.5
items.statement:
Lemma 3.1.5 (1): common finite-memory certificates at two ordered
relaxation endpoints force every intervening reduced image trajectory to
converge to a reduced KKT triple.

Lemma 3.1.5 (2): under common endpoint certificates, the squared primal
residual norms of every intervening exact trajectory are summable.

Lemma 3.1.5 (3): under common endpoint certificates, the squared
second-image increment norms of every intervening exact trajectory are summable.

Lemma 3.1.5 (4): along the reduced-state limit supplied by the interval
certificate, the first reduced objective tilted at its KKT support tends to zero.

Lemma 3.1.5 (5): along the reduced-state limit supplied by the interval
certificate, the second reduced objective tilted at its KKT support tends to zero.
items.title: Lemma 3.1.5

items.label: Notation 3.1.6
items.statement:
Notation 3.1.6 (1): for memory two, the tail-sum formula specializes to
`h₀ = δ₁ + δ₂` and `h₁ = δ₂`.

Notation 3.1.6 (2): the exact Case 1 lag coefficients give the displayed
four-term value storage.

Notation 3.1.6 (3): both current function values have negative coefficients
in Case 1.

Notation 3.1.6 (4): the reconstructed first-block origin-column weights are
the exact pair displayed in the source.

Notation 3.1.6 (5): the first reconstructed flow balance is the negative
current-value coefficient `h_{F,0}`.

Notation 3.1.6 (6): all Case 1 first-block interpolation weights are
nonnegative.

Notation 3.1.6 (7): the lower matrix represents the quadratic remainder.
items.title: Notation 3.1.6

items.label: Proposition 3.1.7
items.statement:
Proposition 3.1.7: The uniform-convergence endpoint is strictly greater than
`377 / 200`.
items.title: Proposition 3.1.7

items.label: Definition 4.1.1
items.statement:
Definition 4.1.1 (1): for cyclic indices modulo `N ≥ 2` and `γ > 0`,
the families `ρ`, `ξ`, `a`, and `c` are respectively `residual`, `xVertex`,
`xNormal`, and `yNormal`.

Definition 4.1.1 (2): a nonself support compares a phase vertex with
the origin or with a vertex at a distinct phase.
items.title: Definition 4.1.1

items.label: Lemma 4.1.2
items.statement:
Lemma 4.1.2 (1): the prescribed cyclic sequences form a unit-penalty consensus
ADMM trajectory for the indicators of the two cycle polytopes.

Lemma 4.1.2 (2): every block minimum along the prescribed trajectory is unique.

Lemma 4.1.2 (3): the origin triple satisfies the consensus KKT conditions.

Lemma 4.1.2 (4): the origin is primal optimal and has objective value zero.

Lemma 4.1.2 (5): a nonzero cycle residual prevents primal-residual convergence
to zero.

Lemma 4.1.2 (6): the positive minimal period of the prescribed trajectory
divides the number of phases.
items.title: Lemma 4.1.2

items.label: Proposition 4.1.3
items.statement:
Proposition 4.1.3: an `N`-periodic consensus ADMM trajectory with a nonzero
residual admits a cyclic projection reduction in dimension at most `2 * N - 2`,
at the same multiplier factor.
items.title: Proposition 4.1.3

items.label: Proposition 4.1.4
items.statement:
Proposition 4.1.4 (1): the canonical positive-semidefinite square-root map
converts the standard Euclidean pairing into a matrix-linear Gram pairing.

Proposition 4.1.4 (2): for fixed coefficient vectors, the Gram support
functional is linear in the matrix argument.

Proposition 4.1.4 (3): simultaneous cyclic invariance makes the three
independent Gram blocks circulant, while positive semidefiniteness identifies
the fourth block as the transpose of the mixed block.

Proposition 4.1.4 (4): finite semidefinite feasibility is equivalent to
the projection-cycle conditions for the two fixed convex hulls under the
canonical square-root realization.
items.title: Proposition 4.1.4

items.label: Definition 4.1.5
items.statement:
Definition 4.1.5: the exact period-48 constants, alternating vector, rank-one
perturbation of the integer matrix, and its parity-dependent support contributions.
items.title: Definition 4.1.5

items.label: Proposition 4.1.6
items.statement:
Proposition 4.1.6 (1): the explicit period-48 Gram matrix H = 2K - I₉₆ + 3hhᵀ is positive definite.

Proposition 4.1.6 (2): the realized cycle data η_i = S e_i, w_i = γ₀⁻¹ S e_{48+i}, ρ_i = w_i - w_{i-1}, ξ_i = η_i + ρ_i, the multiplier vertices ν_i(γ) = γ w_i, and the two hulls.

Proposition 4.1.6, normal formulas: aᵢ(γ) = ηᵢ₋₁ - γ wᵢ₋₁ - ξᵢ and cᵢ(γ) = γ wᵢ₋₁ + ρᵢ.

Proposition 4.1.6 (3): the two convex hulls of the cycle are the fixed polytopes xSet S and ySet S on the critical half-line.

Proposition 4.1.6 (4): the realized families form a projection cycle for every Gram factor and every multiplier on the critical half-line.

Proposition 4.1.6 (5): the prescribed sequences are an indicator-objective consensus ADMM trajectory of exact period 48 on the critical half-line.

Proposition 4.1.6 (6): the residual norm is constant and positive on the critical half-line.

Proposition 4.1.6 (7): at the critical factor every second-block support against the origin or a nonself phase is strict.

Proposition 4.1.6 (8): first-block origin supports are strict, and among nonself phases equality occurs exactly at displacement -10.
items.title: Proposition 4.1.6

items.label: Lemma 5.1.1 / Lemma 5.1.2 / Lemma 5.1.3
items.statement:
Lemma 5.1.1 (1): strictification of a projection cycle with one strict block.

Lemma 5.1.1 (2): the uniform-convergence endpoint lies strictly below the cycle factor.

Lemma 5.1.2 (1): a nontrivial projection cycle with one strict block can be
strictified in dimension at most `2 * N`, while preserving orthogonal cyclic symmetry.

Lemma 5.1.2 (2): a nontrivial projection cycle with one strict block lies
strictly above the uniform-convergence endpoint.

Lemma 5.1.3 (1): strictification of a projection cycle with one strict block.

Lemma 5.1.3 (2): the uniform-convergence endpoint lies strictly below the cycle factor.
items.title: Lemma 5.1.1 / Lemma 5.1.2 / Lemma 5.1.3

items.label: Lemma 5.1.4 / Lemma 5.1.5
items.statement:
Lemma 5.1.4: strict finite projection-cycle data with a nonzero residual admit
smooth strongly convex objectives whose unit-penalty consensus ADMM trajectory is the
prescribed cycle with its exact minimal period, positive constant trajectory value,
globally unique block minimizers, unique KKT triple `(0, 0, 0)`, and optimal value zero.

Lemma 5.1.5: strict finite projection-cycle data with a nonzero residual admit
smooth strongly convex real objectives whose unit-penalty consensus ADMM trajectory
reproduces the prescribed cycle and its exact minimal period, has positive constant
objective value and globally unique block minimizers, and has `(0, 0, 0)` as its
unique KKT triple with optimal value zero.
items.title: Lemma 5.1.4 / Lemma 5.1.5

items.label: Definition 8.1.1
items.statement:
Definition 8.1.1 (1): exact rational cases store the common coefficients,
lag tables, packed interpolation weights, endpoint parameters, and packed endpoint blocks.

Definition 8.1.1 (2): the packed interpolation data reconstruct all weights,
including zero diagonals and the omitted origin column satisfying value balance.

Definition 8.1.1 (3): exact supply matrices and endpoint principal blocks determine
the completed storage matrices through their action on constant histories.

Definition 8.1.1 (4): the exact descent and lower matrices are checked by the
displayed unpivoted `LDLᵀ` recurrence and its strict rational pivot bounds.

Definition 8.1.1 (5): valid endpoint checks produce canonical finite-memory
certificates throughout the closed interval by affine interpolation of `P`.
items.title: Definition 8.1.1

items.label: Notation 9.1.1
items.statement:
Notation 9.1.1: the unscaled integer matrix `K` uses the period-48 convention
`Circ(t) i j = t (j - i)`, the displayed rows `p`, `q`, and `c`, and blocks
`Circ(p)`, `Circ(c)`, `Circ(c)ᵀ`, and `Circ(q)`, with no scaling.
items.title: Notation 9.1.1

items.label: Algorithm 9.1.2
items.statement:
Algorithm 9.1.2: for J₀ = 2K - I₉₆ with K the period-48 two-block integer
matrix, fraction-free elimination starts from B⁽⁰⁾ = J₀ and b₋₁ = 1, and for
k = 0,…,94 updates the trailing entries by
B⁽ᵏ⁺¹⁾ᵢⱼ = (b_k · B⁽ᵏ⁾ᵢⱼ - B⁽ᵏ⁾ᵢₖ · B⁽ᵏ⁾ₖⱼ) / b_{k-1} with b_k = B⁽ᵏ⁾ₖₖ,
where each division is exact in ℤ. The 96 leading principal determinants are
b_0,…,b_94, B⁽⁹⁵⁾₉₅,₉₅, each at least 1, so Sylvester's criterion gives J₀ ≻ 0.
items.title: Algorithm 9.1.2

items.label: Algorithm 9.1.3
items.statement:
Algorithm 9.1.3: for the support tests, form `H = 2K - I₉₆ + 3hhᵀ` by eq:H,
work with the coefficient vectors `ηᵢ = eᵢ` and `wᵢ = e₄₈₊ᵢ / γ₀`, and interpret
every inner product as `zᵀHw`. Set `ρᵢ = wᵢ - wᵢ₋₁`, `ξᵢ = ηᵢ + ρᵢ`, and use the
affine normals `aᵢ(γ) = ηᵢ₋₁ - γ wᵢ₋₁ - ξᵢ` and `cᵢ(γ) = γ wᵢ₋₁ + ρᵢ` of Proposition
prop:fixed. At phase zero the support is evaluated against the origin and against
every other phase, for both blocks. These `96` rational affine expressions give
all `4608` supports by cyclic shifts; their slopes and endpoint values satisfy
Table 2 and the single exceptional expression is eq:active, so the displayed
inputs determine every check needed for Proposition prop:fixed.
items.title: Algorithm 9.1.3

items.label: Proposition prop:finite
items.statement:
The paper's proposition `prop:finite`, including both fixed objective pairs:
the original periodic cycle and the perturbed phase rays with geometric growth.
Each pair has unique finite block minimizers at every input, a zero-valued
origin KKT triple, and the origin as a primal optimum.
items.title: Proposition prop:finite
